$comment: EXAMPLE. Configuration guidance for the Keycloak 26.7.3 image, as a supplier could publish it beside its product record. The record points here under interface-disclosure#R5 from every interface whose certificate is 'deployment-defined', and from the record as a whole. Each entry names the interface by a BOM-Link into the product record, the attribute the operator decides, the setting that decides it, and the supplier's documentation. The option names are Keycloak's; the format is an illustration, not a standard. The CBOM does not carry this content: it changes when the documentation changes, not when the product does.
subject: pkg:oci/keycloak?repository_url=quay.io/keycloak/keycloak&tag=26.7.3

entries.note: The server certificate and key are operator-supplied files. Their algorithm is the interface's authentication value at 'configured'.
The product default is the JDK's group order. A hybrid ML-KEM group can be enabled here only once the JDK in the image supports one.
Defaults to 'inherited': the management listener uses the main server's scheme and certificate. With HTTP on the main server it is plain HTTP.
Off by default. Enabled behind a TLS-terminating proxy, it carries tokens in clear on the proxy hop.
The database server's certificate decides the value; set sslmode=verify-full in the JDBC URL so the driver verifies it.
The product generates and rotates the RSA-2048 key; the operator can switch mutual TLS off, not change the key type.
The realm default is RS256. A client can override it.
